summary:
This research proposes identifying and evaluating terrestrial regions that may serve as partial analogs for the surface materials and certain environmental processes of Mars, with an emphasis on Jezero Crater. The strategy is based on a Martian reference composed of Perseverance/PIXL geochemical data, observations of soil crusts made by Perseverance, and APXS records from the Spirit and Opportunity rovers. This distinction is essential: data from Jezero must not be confused with historical data from other Martian regions.
Based on this reference, a set of terrestrial regions is justified, each representing different components or processes: Puu Waiau and Puu Poliahu on Mauna Kea (Hawaii), Yungay in the Atacama Desert, the VXE-6 site in the McMurdo Dry Valleys, Río Tinto (Spain), Craters of the Moon (Idaho), the Golden Deposit (Canada), Bonneville Salt Flats and Pilot Valley (Utah), Holuhraun (Iceland), and Dallol (Ethiopia). Some of these locations have previously been recognized as analogs; others are incorporated as new candidates in this project’s comparative matrix. The contribution is not to claim the discovery of new analogs, but to organize a selection differentiated by research objective.
details:
Identificar caracteres de la Tierra que presentan características semejantes a determinadas regiones de Marte o la Luna, para utilizarlos como análogos terrestres y estudiar modo preparar futuras misiones de exploración y bases espaciales permanentes.

No se busca encontrar un lugar idénico, sino identificar semejanzas que permiten realizar investigaciones y experimentos útiles.

2. Objetivo general

Identificar y caracterizar sitios terrestres mediante la comparación de sus propiedades químicas, físicas, geológicas, técnicas y ambientales con las de Marte y la Luna, utilizando datos abiertos de NASA y otras agencias espaciales.
